title: Grain Accounting Bulletin: The Bushels a Contract Is Countersigned For
content:
The bushels a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts is countersigned for are the bushels the member applied for or the marketing ceiling, whichever is the smaller, struck in whole bushels, a part bushel taken to the nearest whole bushel and a half bushel taken upward, and never below zero.

**The marketing ceiling.** The marketing ceiling is the member's marketing average taken at the ceiling percentage, with the hauled-load credit added and the forward reserve taken off.

**The marketing average.** The member's marketing average is the bushels the equity ledger held under Membership and Patronage Equity records the member marketing over the last thirty-six months, divided by the production history window the marketing programme carries. Only the bushels the ledger records as marketed business are counted, and the bushels of an allocation posted on them or a retain withheld from them are not counted again.

**The three figures brought to it.** The ceiling percentage is the share of production the member's marketing programme allows to stand sold forward. No hauled-load credit is added. The forward reserve is the standard forward reserve of 3000 bushels.

**Where the striking happens.** The marketing average and the ceiling are each struck in whole bushels, a part bushel taken to the nearest whole bushel and a half bushel taken upward, before the hauled-load credit and the forward reserve are applied to them.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A member applies for 50,000 bushels. The equity ledger records 180,000 bushels of marketed business over the last thirty-six months. Assume the marketing programme carries a production history window of 3 completed crop years and allows 70.0 percent of production to stand sold forward.

| Step | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Bushels marketed over the last thirty-six months | 180,000 |
| Divided by the production history window, struck in whole bushels | 60,000 |
| Taken at the ceiling percentage, struck in whole bushels | 42,000 |
| Hauled-load credit added | nil |
| Forward reserve taken off | 3000 |
| Marketing ceiling | 39,000 |
| Bushels applied for | 50,000 |

The smaller of the two is the marketing ceiling, so the contract is countersigned for 39,000 bushels. Had the ceiling before the striking come to 41,999.50, it would be struck at 42,000, the half bushel being taken upward.
